results.title: Graph Neural Networks based Analog Circuit Link Prediction
results.content: GNN-ACLP: Graph Neural Networks based Analog Circuit Link Prediction. Circuit link prediction identifying missing component connections from incomplete netlists is crucial in automating analog circuit design. However, existing methods face three main challenges: 1) Insufficient use of topological patterns in circuit graphs reduces prediction accuracy; 2) Data scarcity due to the complexity of annotations hinders model generalization; 3) Limited adaptability to various netlist formats. First, we introduce the SEAL (Subgraphs, Embeddings, and Attributes for Link Prediction) framework and achieve port-level accuracy in circuit link prediction. To address these, the authors propose GNN-ACLP, a novel framework that integrates GNNs with the SEAL (Subgraphs, Embeddings, and Attributes for Link Prediction) methodology for port-level link prediction. The circuit link prediction problem is formally defined as a graph-based task where nodes represent component ports and edges denote connections. This is framed as Problem 2.2 in the paper, where a node is removed from the graph and its neighbors must be predicted based on the remaining structure and the known component type.

results.content: To address these challenges, we propose GNN-ACLP, a GNNs-based method for analog circuit link prediction, as illustrated in Figure 1, and SpiceNetlist, a large-scale netlist dataset, whose statistic is demonstrated in Table 1. GNN-ACLP, a port-level accurate circuit link prediction method based on the SEAL framework using graph neural networks (GNNs). SpiceNetlist, a novel circuit netlist dataset comprising 775 annotated circuits in both SPICE and JSON formats, featuring 10 component types to facilitate the training and evaluation of circuit link prediction methods. We adopt the SEAL framework for link prediction in circuit graphs and train it using DRNL one-hot encoding combined with the original component node features. For the circuit-link-prediction problem, there are very few datasets available, and the existing ones do not contain enough readily accessible netlists for practical training and evaluation. We propose GNN-ACLP, a novel graph neural networks based framework with SEAL framework integration and achieve port-level accuracy in analog circuit link prediction.
